title: Documents & files
intro: Every property keeps its files in its own folder — T12s, rent rolls, agreements, anything. Add them on the property’s page; a T12 is checked by the app’s reader and by the AI before it is used, and a file with several properties’ parts is never used until you say which part is whose.

topics.title: A property’s Documents
topics.intro: On every property’s page (with or without a loan): the files saved for that property. The assistant reads them when you talk about the property, so you never upload a file twice.

steps.title: Documents
steps.text: A new property has no documents yet. Add files with the button, or drag them from your folder onto this box.

marks.label: Documents
marks.text: The files saved in this property’s folder.

marks.label: Saved for …
marks.text: Which property — the assistant reads these when you focus it.

marks.label: What you are adding
marks.text: The type of the next files you add (next step). “Detect automatically” looks at what is in the file.

marks.label: Add files
marks.text: Opens your computer’s file window: pick one or more files and click Open. Dropping files on this box does the same.

marks.label: Nothing yet
marks.text: Shown until the first file is added.

steps.title: What you are adding
steps.text: Pick the type before you add a file when you know it; otherwise leave “Detect automatically”. A file added as a type is saved to this property as that type.

marks.label: Detect automatically
marks.text: The app reads the file and decides: a T12, a rent roll, an agreement… A file that names another property is filed there instead.

marks.label: Loan agreement
marks.text: The loan agreement — read when you ask to fill in the loan from it.

marks.label: T12
marks.text: The operating statement. It goes through the T12 check before it is used (next topic).

marks.label: Rent roll
marks.text: The rent roll: units, occupancy and rents.

marks.label: Unit Statistics
marks.text: A unit statistics report.

marks.label: Other
marks.text: Anything else — kept and read by the assistant, used for no figure.

steps.title: A file in the list
steps.text: Here a made-up loan agreement was added as “Loan agreement”. Each file is a row: its name, size and the day it was saved, its type, and two buttons. A file with the same name but different content is kept as a copy (“… (2)”), never replaced; the same file twice says “Already on file”.

marks.label: The file
marks.text: Its name as you saved it.

marks.label: Size · saved
marks.text: Its size and the day it was saved (“no readable text” when the app can’t read any — a picture-only file is read by OCR, see “Scanned PDFs”).

marks.label: How it was read
marks.text: How much text was read from it (or, for a PDF, its pages and which were read by OCR).

marks.label: Type
marks.text: What the file is. Change it here at any time (topic “Change or remove a file”).

marks.label: Save copy
marks.text: Saves a copy of the file wherever you choose on your computer (your computer’s save window opens).

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Deletes it from the property’s folder — asks first.

marks.label: Folder
marks.text: Opens the documents folder on your computer.

topics.title: Add a T12: the check
topics.intro: A T12 is read twice — by the app’s own reader and by the AI (Claude) — before anything from it is used. When every check passes and the AI agrees, it is used at once. Otherwise this window opens and you decide.

steps.title: The review window
steps.text: A made-up T12 added with “Detect automatically”. Every check of the reader passes, but the AI reads two rows differently — so it waits for you. Nothing is saved or used until you click Save.

marks.label: Review the T12 reading — …
marks.text: The property it is for.

marks.label: The file and sheet
marks.text: Rows and columns are numbered as Excel numbers them, so you can find each one in the file.

marks.label: The verdict
marks.text: How many of the reader’s checks fail (or “every check passes”), and whether the AI agrees.
Closes the window without saving — like Keep it waiting.

marks.label: Income · Expenses · NOI
marks.text: The accounts added up, against the totals the statement prints: ✓ when they match, ✗ in red when they don’t.

marks.label: What to look at
marks.text: Every failed check (red) and every point where the AI reads it differently (amber), with its row.

marks.label: The rows
marks.text: Every row of the file and what the reader made of it (next steps).

marks.label: Keep it waiting
marks.text: Closes the window. The T12 waits — unused — in Documents, Underwriting and Data Health.

marks.label: Save this reading
marks.text: Saves the reading with your changes; its figures are used everywhere.

steps.title: How each row was read
steps.text: One line per row of the file. The file’s own name column comes first, then what the reader made of the row; the months and the total, as in the file, are further right (scroll the table sideways).

marks.label: Row
marks.text: The row number in Excel.

marks.label: What the reader made of it
marks.text: Account, Category name, Total, Income total, Expense total, Net Operating Income, Not operating — or Above the header, Header row, Empty.

marks.label: Side
marks.text: Income or Expense (accounts only).

marks.label: Category (in the file)
marks.text: The category the account sits under in the file itself.

marks.label: Underwriting line
marks.text: The line of the Underwriting table it adds to (with the item it is, e.g. “the vacancy”, under it).

marks.label: Amount used
marks.text: The amount the reader takes (grey). Type another to use yours — it then needs a note.

marks.label: Your note
marks.text: Why you changed this row.

marks.label: Check
marks.text: ✓ = its months add up to its total. A failed check is in red; the AI’s point in amber.

steps.title: Where the AI disagrees
steps.text: Click a row number in the list on top: the table jumps to that row, lit up. Here the AI puts “Utility Reimbursements” on the expense side; the reader has it as income. Decide which is right from the file — change the row, or leave it.

marks.label: Row 17
marks.text: Jumps to the row.

marks.label: The row
marks.text: Amber: the AI reads it differently.

marks.label: Side
marks.text: Income here; the AI says Expense. Change it if the AI is right.

marks.label: AI: …
marks.text: What the AI read.

steps.title: Change a row
steps.text: Change any list on a row and the window works out the checks again at once. Here Utility Reimbursements is moved from Other Income to its own underwriting line, Utility Reimbursements (RUBS). A row you changed is marked “yours”, and the footer counts your changes (“clear my changes” undoes them all).

marks.label: Underwriting line
marks.text: Changed by you…

marks.label: yours
marks.text: …so it is marked as your decision.

marks.label: 1 change of yours · clear my changes
marks.text: How many changes you made; the link undoes them all.

marks.label: The verdict
marks.text: Worked out again with your change.

steps.title: A different amount needs a note
steps.text: Type an amount on a row to use it instead of the file’s: here the AI’s reading of Plumbing Repairs. The box turns green and the note box red — an amount that differs from the file can’t be saved without a note saying why.

marks.label: Amount used
marks.text: Your amount (green).

marks.label: why (needed)
marks.text: Red until you write why. Save says which row still needs a note.

marks.label: AI: …
marks.text: The AI’s reading of this row (the total, and the month it reads differently).

marks.label: The verdict
marks.text: With your amount the expenses no longer add up to the totals the statement prints, so those checks now fail.

marks.label: A failed check
marks.text: Red: a total the statement prints that its rows no longer add up to (and by how much).

steps.title: The note
steps.text: Write why in the note box and click elsewhere. The note is kept with the reading and in the property’s change history.

marks.label: Your note
marks.text: Why the amount differs.

marks.label: 1 change of yours
marks.text: Your change, ready to save.

marks.label: Save this reading
marks.text: Saves it (next step).

steps.title: Some checks still fail
steps.text: Save while a check fails and the app asks first. Saved anyway, your accounts are used as you set them (or, if you changed no figure, the statement’s printed totals, with the difference shown in Underwriting).

marks.label: Some checks still fail
marks.text: How many checks fail.

marks.label: What is used
marks.text: Which figures are used if you save anyway.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Back to the window to fix the rows.

marks.label: Save anyway
marks.text: Saves the reading as it is; it is used everywhere.

topics.title: Waiting for your review
topics.intro: “Keep it waiting” closes the window: the T12 is kept, but nothing from it is used until you review it.

steps.title: In Documents
steps.text: The T12’s row says it is waiting, with a Review button that opens the same window.

marks.label: The T12
marks.text: Saved in the folder…

marks.label: T12: Waiting for your review
marks.text: …but not used yet.

marks.label: Review
marks.text: Opens the review window.

marks.label: Type: T12
marks.text: Detected as a T12.

steps.title: In Underwriting
steps.text: Underwriting shows it too, above the property’s figures, and Data Health lists it under “T12s that need your review”.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: The property.

marks.label: … is waiting for your review
marks.text: The file, why it waits, and that nothing from it is used yet.

marks.label: Review
marks.text: Opens the review window.

steps.title: Reviewed
steps.text: Open Review, look at the rows and click “Save this reading” (no change was needed here). The T12 is used at once: its NOI reaches the property page, Home, the debt sizing and the refinance.

marks.label: T12: Reviewed by you
marks.text: In use. Other words you may see: “Checked by the reader and the AI” (both agreed), “Read by the reader only (Claude wasn’t connected)”, “Being read…”.

topics.title: Change or remove a file
topics.intro: Every file’s type can be changed, and every file can be removed — always with a question first.

steps.title: Change its type
steps.text: Pick another type in the row’s list. Making a file a T12 sends it through the T12 check; taking the T12 type away from the T12 in use rebuilds the property’s numbers from any other T12 on file.

marks.label: Loan agreement
marks.text: Its type now.

marks.label: T12
marks.text: Read and checked as a T12.

marks.label: Rent roll
marks.text: Read as the rent roll.

marks.label: Unit Statistics
marks.text: A unit statistics report.

marks.label: Other
marks.text: Kept, used for no figure.

steps.title: Remove — the question
steps.text: Remove always asks. Removing the T12 in use says what goes with it: its NOI leaves Home, the DSCR and the refinance, and the numbers are rebuilt from any other T12 on file (otherwise the property has no NOI yet). The automatic backups keep a copy of every removed file (Settings → Backups).

marks.label: Remove “…”?
marks.text: The file.

marks.label: What goes with it
marks.text: Deleted from the property’s folder; for the T12 in use, its NOI too.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps the file.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Deletes it and rebuilds the property’s numbers.

topics.title: One file, several properties
topics.intro: A workbook can hold several properties’ statements — one per sheet, or one after another. Added anywhere, it never goes anywhere by itself: you say which part is whose.

steps.title: Which part is whose?
steps.text: Added on Sample Gardens’ page, a made-up workbook with three sheets. The app suggests a property for each part whose name matches one; check them, change anything, then approve.

marks.label: The file
marks.text: How many parts and sheets, and which parts are already set to this property.

marks.label: Part 1
marks.text: Sheet 1 of 3 · its sheet name · the property name in it; what it is (T12) and its NOI.

marks.label: Ticked
marks.text: This part will be linked.

marks.label: This property
marks.text: Set to Sample Gardens: its name matches.

marks.label: Another property
marks.text: Part 2 names Sample Oaks — it goes to Sample Oaks’ folder.

marks.label: Not linked
marks.text: Maple Court is no property in the app: not ticked, “Don’t link”.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing is saved.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: Saves the file to each property with its own part.

steps.title: More choices
steps.text: Each list offers Don’t link, this property, every other property, and “Add as a new property” named after the part. “+ another property” adds a second list: the same part then goes to both (one agreement over two properties, say). Two parts given to one property are added together.

marks.label: A second property
marks.text: Added by “+ another property” — pick the second property, or leave it empty.

marks.label: ➕ Add as a new property “Maple Court”
marks.text: Creates that property and links this part to it.

marks.label: Ticked by itself
marks.text: Picking a property ticks the part.

steps.title: Each property, its own part
steps.text: Here part 3 is set back to “Don’t link” and the extra list emptied, then Approve. Each T12 part goes through the T12 check for its property. The file’s row says which part is this property’s, with Change to answer again.

marks.label: This property’s part: …
marks.text: Which sheet of the file is Sample Gardens’ — only its numbers are read for it.

marks.label: Change
marks.text: Opens the question again to give another answer.

marks.label: T12: …
marks.text: Its part went through the T12 check (here it waits for review, like any T12).

steps.title: Waiting for your answer
steps.text: A file saved before the question was asked (or by the assistant) waits for an answer: none of its numbers are used for this property until you say which part is its own. Data Health lists every such file.

marks.label: It has 3 parts — which one is this property’s?
marks.text: Its numbers aren’t used until you say.

marks.label: Answer
marks.text: Opens the question (next step).

steps.title: Answer
steps.text: When no part names this property, nothing is set for you: tick its part and pick this property, then Approve — or Cancel and answer later.

marks.label: Which part is Sample Pines (example)’s?
marks.text: Pick it below — nothing is set for you.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: Pick “Sample Pines (example) (this property)” on the right part.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: The file keeps waiting.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: Links the part; its numbers are used from now on.

topics.title: A T12 that names no property
topics.intro: A T12 added on a property’s page whose sheet doesn’t name that property: the app asks which sheet is its T12, or keeps the file as a plain document.

steps.title: Which sheet is its T12?
steps.text: Pick the sheet that is this property’s T12 and click “Save it” (it then goes through the T12 check) — or pick “None — keep it as a document”.

marks.label: Which sheet is … ’s T12?
marks.text: The property you are on.

marks.label: Why it asks
marks.text: The file doesn’t name this property.

marks.label: A sheet
marks.text: Use this sheet as the property’s T12.

marks.label: None — keep it as a document
marks.text: Saved as an “Other” document; no figure is taken from it.

marks.label: Save it
marks.text: Saves the file with your answer.

topics.title: Scanned PDFs
topics.intro: A PDF is read page by page. A page that is a picture (a scan) is read by OCR — the computer reads the letters from the picture — which may make mistakes, so the app always says which pages were read that way.

steps.title: Reading…
steps.text: While a file is read, a small card at the bottom left shows its progress page by page. You can keep working. If the app is closed halfway, it goes on reading at the next start.

marks.label: The reading card
marks.text: One card per file being read.

marks.label: The file
marks.text: Its name.

marks.label: reading scanned page 2 of 2
marks.text: Which page it is on; “scanned page” = read by OCR.

marks.label: Stop
marks.text: Stops after this page. Nothing is saved; add the file again to go on where it stopped (pages already read are kept).

steps.title: Read
steps.text: Once read, the file is saved and its row says how it was read. A PDF also gets “Pages & properties”.

marks.label: 2 pages · page 2 read by OCR — may contain errors
marks.text: How it was read: pages read by OCR (amber), and any page that couldn’t be read.

marks.label: Pages & properties
marks.text: Split the PDF by pages, or link it to several properties (next step).

steps.title: Pages & properties
steps.text: One PDF can hold several agreements (split it into parts by pages), or one agreement can cover several properties (give the part to each). Each property reads only its own pages.

marks.label: Which pages belong to which property?
marks.text: The file and how many pages.

marks.label: Pages … to …
marks.text: The part’s first and last page.

marks.label: What it is
marks.text: An optional name for the part (e.g. Loan agreement, Phase 1).
Removes the part.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: The property this part belongs to.

marks.label: + another property
marks.text: The same pages go to a second property too.

marks.label: + Add a part (pages)
marks.text: Another page range, for another property.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

marks.label: Approve
marks.text: Saves the parts; the file is copied to each property named.

topics.title: When Claude isn’t connected
topics.intro: Without Claude the AI can’t read the T12, so it can’t be checked against the reader. The app asks what to do.

steps.title: Claude isn’t connected
steps.text: A made-up T12 added while Claude is signed out. Nothing from it is used yet.

marks.label: Claude isn’t connected
marks.text: (“The AI couldn’t read this T12” when Claude is connected but its reading failed.)

marks.label: The file
marks.text: Which property and file, and that it hasn’t been checked.

marks.label: The reader’s checks
marks.text: Whether the app’s own reader passes every check.

marks.label: Keep it waiting
marks.text: Kept, unused, until you review it (or Claude is back and you read it again).

marks.label: Use the reader’s reading
marks.text: Only when every check passes: used as the reader read it.

marks.label: Review it myself
marks.text: Opens the review window.

steps.title: Used as the reader read it
steps.text: After “Use the reader’s reading” the T12 is in use, and its row says it was read by the reader only.

marks.label: T12: Read by the reader only (Claude wasn’t connected)
marks.text: In use without the AI’s check. Reading it again once Claude is connected (Underwriting → Read again) checks it with the AI.
